A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SigmaDock and contain readable main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–J. Content can be matched across the revised pagination and relocated displays.

before.justification: v1 reports original docking benchmarks, component ablations, conformational-alignment experiments, generated poses, and sampling-efficiency analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds pocket-cutoff sensitivity results and a Vina pocket-size control in Section 3.2.

M1.justification: FR3D, the SE(3) diffusion objective, EquiformerV2 backbone, prediction head, and sampling/ranking procedures remain unchanged. Expanded descriptions clarify existing components; the RDKit reference distances and pseudo-force construction were already documented in v1 Appendix G.

E1.justification: Both versions train on PDBBind(v2020) and evaluate known-pocket redocking on PoseBusters and Astex. The added pocket-cutoff sweep varies preprocessing within retained coverage. Flexible docking, cross-docking, and co-folding remain unevaluated.

E2.justification: Section 3.2 adds a numerical comparison with DiffDock-L, citing its 50% RMSD-only Top-1 result and larger training corpus. This is a literature-result comparison, not a newly documented matched evaluation. Figure 4 retains its comparator set; Vina and AF3 were already compared in v1.

E3.justification: The new sensitivity experiment sweeps pocket cutoffs from 4 to 7 Å while reducing cutoff jitter toward zero, and adds a Vina control using autobox plus 5 Å. The reported failure criterion is corrected from majority RMSD below 2 Å to above 2 Å, without changing Table 2 values or establishing a rerun. Existing training and default sampling settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 3 tests sensitivity to pocket size, and the Vina control examines whether pocket definitions explain SigmaDock's advantage. Existing component ablations, cofactor analysis, alignment studies, generated-pose cases, and sampling-efficiency analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain Table 2's averaging across 40 seeds and Figure 12's permutation means and standard-deviation shading. No new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds pocket-sweep PB-valid success rates of 80.2%, 80.5%, 77.3%, and 68.2% for 4–7 Å cutoffs, plus Vina's 57.2% versus 56.0% control comparison. Appendix J revises AF3 stratum scores from 86/80/79 to 87/82/78 and its average from 80.1% to 80.2%. The abstract's comparator upper value changes from 30.8% to 32.8%; FR3D's reported reduction changes from approximately 66% removed to two-thirds retained. Existing SigmaDock benchmark and ablation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix D.4 adds a constrained-manifold definition, Jacobian-rank dimension argument, and effective degrees-of-freedom bounds; Section 2.2.3 corrects the fragment-count lower bound from zero to one. Existing theorems and proofs remain. The added derivation is internally inconsistent: a constraint map with 2e outputs cannot have Jacobian rank 5e for e > 0.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion explicitly qualify the superiority claim as known-pocket, rigid-receptor redocking and add co-folding as a proposed future extension. The redocking restriction already appeared in v1 Appendix J.1, so this is a limited refinement of headline scope. The central methodological and performance claims persist.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new pocket experiments as evidence that smaller pockets do not explain the performance advantage. It also expands the explanation distinguishing noise-induced correlations from correlations learned by the score model and motivates redocking through industrial screening practice. Appendix J.1's substantive limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds explicit post-sampling dummy-removal and bond-reconstruction details and a reproducibility statement naming the intended code repository. v1 only promised code and weights after review. The new statement still describes a future release; actual availability is not established by the PDFs. Existing hardware, training budgets, and hyperparameters remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Corso et al. (2024) for DiffDock-L and Ryckaert et al. (1977) for holonomic constraints, and expands discussion of comparison fairness across redocking and co-folding. The dedicated related-work appendix otherwise remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites expand the introduction, fragmentation explanation, experimental discussion, and conclusion. A reproducibility section and correspondence information are added, and the preprint header becomes an ICLR 2026 publication header. The overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the pocket-sensitivity Table 3 and a compact main-text redisplay of the existing AF3 comparison as Table 4; the appendix comparison becomes Table 5. Figures and algorithms are retained with some relocation, and Table 1 gains a default-configuration marker. The visual changes are localized.

improvement.justification: The pocket-sensitivity experiment, Vina control, clearer headline scope, corrected failure definition, and repository information improve evidence and transparency. However, the new Appendix D.4 derivation claims rank 5(m−1) for a constraint Jacobian with only 2(m−1) rows, weakening its theoretical justification. Revised Table 5 also displays 72−87 as −16 rather than −15. These useful additions coexist with newly introduced mathematical and numerical errors, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
